terms.meaning: A stored proof that a user is signed in, so they do not need to sign in again.
A temporary user with no real account, who can still try the app.
A piece of code that waits for an event and reacts when it happens.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Loads the state library and the cloud connection.
sections.why: Needed for storing state and talking to the cloud.

sections.name: AuthUser
sections.title: User shape
sections.what: Describes one user: id, email, name, role, optional picture, and creation time.
sections.why: Gives every screen the same user information.

sections.name: AuthState
sections.title: Available auth actions
sections.what: Lists what the store can do: register, log in, log in as guest, log out, edit profile, and start up.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: defaultGuestUser
sections.title: Built-in guest user
sections.what: A ready-made guest profile used when no real user exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets someone preview the app without an account.
sections.watch_out: The guest email is a placeholder address, so do not treat it as a real account.

sections.name: useAuthStore (part 1)
sections.title: Startup session check
sections.what: At startup, uses the real user if the cloud has a session, otherwise uses the guest. Also starts listening for cloud sign-in and sign-out changes.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets someone preview the app before signing in.
sections.watch_out: Each startup adds a listener that is never removed, and development strict mode can start it twice.

sections.name: useAuthStore: if
sections.title: Sign-in change handling and sign-up start
sections.what: Updates the signed-in user when the cloud reports a change, then begins sign-up by checking the fields and creating a local user when the cloud is not set up.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the signed-in state in step with the cloud.
sections.watch_out: The default role here differs from the default used in other places, so new users may get different roles.

sections.name: useAuthStore: if
sections.title: Sign-up result and sign-in start
sections.what: Shows cloud sign-up errors, stores the new user on success, then starts sign-in and creates a local demo user when the cloud is not set up.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives clear feedback and a working preview without the cloud.
sections.watch_out: Local sign-in accepts any email and password, so it gives no real protection.

sections.name: useAuthStore: if
sections.title: Sign-in result, guest, sign-out and profile edits
sections.what: Stores the signed-in user after cloud sign-in, provides guest access, clears the user on sign-out, and merges profile edits into the current user.
sections.why: Likely reason: completes the sign-in lifecycle.
sections.watch_out: Profile edits change only the local copy and are not sent to the cloud.

summary: Keeps track of who is signed in, and handles sign-up, sign-in, guest access, sign-out and profile edits.
purpose: Decides whether the user sees the app or the login screen, and stores the user's name and role.
why: Likely reason: one shared place for sign-in state keeps every screen consistent.
how: 1) Starts as a guest who is signed in. 2) At startup, checks for a real cloud session, otherwise stays a guest. 3) Listens for cloud sign-in and sign-out changes. 4) Sign-up and sign-in use the cloud if configured, otherwise create a local user. 5) Sign-out clears the user.
inputs: Email, password, name and role from the login screen, and the cloud session.
outputs: The current user and the signed-in flag used by the page.
risks: The store starts signed in as a guest, so the login screen only appears after sign-out. Local sign-in accepts any password. Profile edits are not saved to the cloud.
debug: If the login screen never shows, check the initial signed-in value. If sign-in fails, check the error message returned from the cloud. If changes disappear on reload, check whether profile updates were saved.
